Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins issued on 10th May 2008 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2008” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock of the coin.
The Southern Ridges of Singapore consist of Mount Faber, Telok Blangah Hill and Kent Ridge. A series of pedestrian linkages connecting the ridges all the way to Labrador Nature Reserve will enable one to enjoy the panoramic views and nature along the way.
• Mount Faber
At 105 metres above sea-level, Mount Faber is Singapore’s second highest hill after Bukit Timah Hill. Also one of the oldest parks in Singapore, Mount Faber is a popular leisure destination where visitors can enjoy breathtaking views of the southern part of Singapore and the southern islands, or ride on a cable car to Sentosa.
The coin features a beautiful creation atop the hill, namely the attractively adorned Jewel Box Station, where visitors board the cable cars or stop by for food and refreshments at the restaurants and cafes inside. The familiar cable cars across the skyline are in the background.
• Telok Blangah Hill Park
Telok Blangah Hill Park is a historical place of gathering for trading communities who flourished at the site since the early 19th century. The prosperity of the traders is symbolised by Alkaff Mansion — an elegant colonial bungalow built by an Arab trader to entertain guests of different races. Another key feature of the Park is the Terrace Garden, a popular spot for wedding couples and where one can enjoy a panoramic 360-degree view of Singapore.
The coin captures the grandeur of Alkaff Mansion surrounded by the serenity of the Terrace Garden with its semi-circled terraces decked with lovely bougainvilleas in full bloom.
• Kent Ridge Park
The 47 hectare Kent Ridge Park boasts a heritage trail with a 280-metre long canopy walk amidst the lush greenery. Also located at the Park is the Reflections at Bukit Chandu Museum, built in memory of our brave warriors who fought one of the last battles of Singapore here during World War II, and to recount the history of Singapore during the war.
Depicted on the coin is the Reflections at Bukit Chandu Museum, with a group of visiting school children and teachers. The Park’s heritage trail, which is popular with nature lovers and fitness enthusiasts, is also featured on the coin.

• Labrador Nature Reserve
The 16.8 hectare Labrador Nature Reserve is home to the Labrador Park. With its World War II relics, it is an oasis of tranquility and nature’s wonder that offers a picturesque view of the sea.
Featured on the coin are the 2 most recognisable symbols at the Park, namely, the Berlayer Red Beacon and a replica of the Dragon’s Teeth Gate, both of which were, for hundreds of years, navigational aids to Asian and early European sailors and traders sailing past Singapore. Also depicted is the Labrador Jetty, a favorite spot for anglers and those who simply enjoy watching cruise ships sail past.
A standard feature of each coin is the architectural designs of 2 key pedestrian bridges at the Southern Ridges: the 80-metre long Alexandra Arch across Alexandra Road which connects to the 1.6-kilometre long elevated walkway leading to Telok Blangah Hill Park; and the 274-metre long Henderson Waves, which spans across Henderson Road to connect Telok Blangah Hill Park to Mount Faber Park.
The denomination of the coin in figures is to the right of the main design on all the coins.
